consumer: The frontend tile renderer deciding how to shade each tile, asking 'is this tile remembered-but-not-currently-visible so it should be drawn dimmed (vs fully lit if seen, vs blank if never known)?'
scope: Per-tile display state across the rendered/remembered map view: the three-way visible / remembered-dimmed / unknown distinction the GUI draws, not just raw current line-of-sight.
decisive_source: src/arcopolis_export.cpp::write_tiles writes seen=map::pl_sees(p,radius); map::pl_sees is a current-line-of-sight predicate (can the player SEE the tile now), which has no notion of the avatar's remembered/memorized map tiles.
divergence: A tile the avatar previously walked past and memorized but now stands behind a wall: the GUI displays it DIMMED (remembered), but pl_sees returns false (cannot currently see), so the surface reports it identically to a never-seen unknown tile and the dimmed-remembered shading can never be reproduced.
